strengths: Addresses a well-motivated and practically important problem: unifying complementary text-based and visually-grounded reasoning modes into a single adaptive model rather than specializing in one domain.

Technically sound extension of GRPO (AdaGRPO) with three clearly motivated components (prefix-guided exploration, mode-relative advantage via Gaussian CDF estimation, curriculum data scheduling), each individually ablated in Table 3.

Extensive empirical validation across 8 diverse benchmarks (math, spatial, hallucination, general) and two model scales (3B/7B), with AdaVaR-7B surpassing GPT-4o on average and consistently beating the Qwen2.5-VL baseline on every benchmark, unlike compared single-mode methods.

Thorough analysis section: mode-selection behavior across fine-grained categories, attention visualization justifying mode choice, error decomposition into selection vs. reasoning errors, comparison against naive ensemble baselines (Expert Pick, Max(GRD,TXT)) showing the learned policy is genuinely better than heuristic routing.

Strong reproducibility effort: detailed prompts, data construction pipeline, hyperparameters, and an SFT-only ablation (Appendix C.2) that convincingly shows mode selection cannot be reliably learned without the online RL stage.
Efficiency analysis (theoretical FLOPs and wall-clock time) shows AdaGRPO adds negligible overhead over vanilla GRPO by sharing KV cache across mode prefixes.
weaknesses: The core algorithmic novelty is an incremental extension of GRPO (adding token-position-specific advantages and a Gaussian-CDF-based pairwise preference term); the Gaussian independence assumption used to derive mode-relative advantage is not itself validated against alternative estimators.

On several individual benchmarks (e.g., MathVision, MathVerse) specialist text-based models like OVR-7B substantially outperform AdaVaR-7B, so the 'general' model's aggregate gain partly reflects averaging rather than uniformly strong performance; the equal-weighting average schema across benchmarks of very different sizes/difficulties is not well justified.
Many baseline numbers are self-reproduced (marked with *) rather than taken from original papers, which could introduce evaluation inconsistencies or unintentional advantages for the proposed method.

The reasoning-mode taxonomy is limited to only two modes in the main experiments; while width/depth extensions are discussed in the appendix, no actual experiments demonstrate scalability beyond two modes, leaving the generality of the MoVT paradigm partly speculative.

Data construction relies on a fairly complex, multi-stage pipeline (distillation from Orsta, GPT-4o/Qwen-72B based filtering and re-formatting) whose quality is validated only via small-scale spot checks (100 samples), raising some concern about label/data noise propagating into training.

No variance/multiple-seed results are reported for the RL training, which is known to be sensitive to random seeds and rollout sampling, making it hard to assess the statistical robustness of the reported gains.
